literal: Even a tiny bit good things let one listen to, to that same extent abundant greatness it will yield.
translation: Let a person listen to good things, however small they may be; even to that small extent, it will yield abundant greatness.
modern: எவ்வளவு சிறிதளவாக இருந்தாலும் நல்ல விஷயங்களைக் கேட்க வேண்டும்; அந்தக் கேட்ட அளவிற்கு அது நிறைந்த பெருமையைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the immense value of listening to wise and virtuous words, regardless of how brief or small the instruction might be. The poet uses the correlative terms 'எனைத்தானும்' (however small) and 'அனைத்தானும்' (to that very extent) to show a direct proportion between listening and gaining dignity. Even a tiny drop of good advice, when heard and absorbed, translates into a corresponding measure of deep, abundant greatness for the listener. Therefore, one should never dismiss good words as insignificant, for every bit of listening contributes to one's character.
